title: Ruby Performance Fundamentals
subtopics: Optimizing measured problems rather than guesses
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of ruby performance fundamentals in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply ruby performance fundamentals in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to optimizing measured problems rather than guesses and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Ruby Performance Fundamentals through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding ruby performance fundamentals helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Ruby Performance Fundamentals helps you reason about establishing a baseline. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Establishing a baseline. Then connect it to Finding bottlenecks. The remaining syllabus points—Optimizing measured problems rather than guesses—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports ruby performance fundamentals. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for ruby performance fundamentals using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Optimizing measured problems rather than guesses), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain ruby performance fundamentals, identify its place in performance and memory management, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
